'''Enrica Bordignon''' (born 5 April 1975) is an Italian chemist and Chair of Electron Spin Resonance at the [[University of Geneva]]. Her research involves the development of [[EPR spectroscopy|electron paramagnetic resonance]] to study membrane potentials.

== Early life and education ==
Bordignon was an undergraduate student and doctoral researcher at the [[University of Padua]]. Her doctoral research investigated the photo-physical properties of reaction centres in antenna complexes.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=IRTG summer school & 6th Westerberger Herbsttagung |url=https://www.biologie.uni-osnabrueck.de/fileadmin/Medien/SFB/pdf_IRTG/IRTG_Summer_School_2012_Abstract_Book.pdf}}</ref> During her doctorate, she worked at Berlin's Max Volmer Laboratory. She completed her undergraduate studies ''[[summa cum laude]]'' in 1999. She was a postdoctoral researcher at the [[Osnabrück University]] and [[ETH Zurich]].<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |date=2019-11-18 |title=Enrica Bordignon - Bordignon Research Group - UNIGE |url=https://www.unige.ch/sciences/chifi/bordignon/members/enrica-bordignon |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=www.unige.ch |language=en}}</ref> At Osnabrück Bordignon studied bacterial photoaxis membrane protein complexes (including [[Neuropeptide S receptor]]s) and [[ABC-transporter]]s (including [[Escherichia coli]]) using spin labelling.<ref name=":0" /> At Zurich Bordignon continued to apply spin labelling to investigate the [[ATP-binding cassette transporter]]s, including BtuCD-F [[vitamin B12]] importer.<ref name=":0" />

== Research and career ==
In 2013 Bordignon was made a professor of biophysics at the [[Free University of Berlin]]. Her research uses site-directed spin labelling [[Electron paramagnetic resonance|EPR]] to understand the dynamics and conformational changes of membrane proteins. Membrane proteins are the targets of many pharmaceuticals. Transporter membranes move substances in and out of the cellular environment.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Innovative Method To Observe Cell Transport Developed |url=http://www.technologynetworks.com/cell-science/news/innovative-method-to-observe-cell-transport-developed-366950 |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=Cell Science from Technology Networks |language=en}}</ref> Bordignon has shown that EPR can be used to study membrane potentials ''[[in situ]]'', i.e. in cells.  She has particularly developed double electron–electron resonance (DEER), which can be used to monitor one system of spins while exciting another set of spins at a second microwave frequency.<ref>{{Citation |last=Galazzo |first=Laura |chapter=Orthogonal spin labeling and pulsed dipolar spectroscopy for protein studies |date=2022 |chapter-url=https://linkinghub.elsevier.com/retrieve/pii/S0076687922000350 |title=Methods in Enzymology |volume=666 |pages=79–119 |access-date=2023-11-19 |publisher=Elsevier |language=en |doi=10.1016/bs.mie.2022.02.004 |isbn=978-0-323-99974-8 |last2=Teucher |first2=Markus |last3=Bordignon |first3=Enrica|chapter-url-access=subscription }}</ref> She was the first to use spin-labelled nanobodies to report cellular membrane potentials.<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Galazzo |first=Laura |last2=Meier |first2=Gianmarco |last3=Timachi |first3=M. Hadi |last4=Hutter |first4=Cedric A. J. |last5=Seeger |first5=Markus A. |last6=Bordignon |first6=Enrica |date=2020-02-04 |title=Spin-labeled nanobodies as protein conformational reporters for electron paramagnetic resonance in cellular membranes |url=https://pnas.org/doi/full/10.1073/pnas.1913737117 |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=117 |issue=5 |pages=2441–2448 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1913737117 |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=7007536 |pmid=31964841}}</ref> She moved to the [[Ruhr University Bochum]] in 2016. She was appointed Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of Geneva]] in 2021, and made Vice Dean for Science in 2023.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2007-12-10 |title=Dean's Office - Faculté des sciences |url=https://www.unige.ch/sciences/en/lafaculte/organisation/decanat/ |access-date=2023-11-19 |website=www.unige.ch |language=en}}</ref>
